text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 23,810.85, up 1.58% on the day and 4.66% over the past five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.25% (3.61% five‑day). Advances outnumbered declines sharply (401 vs 92), but the breadth score remains weak at 28.9, with only about 28% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average. The market’s rally was broad‑based, driven by gains in IT, pharma, healthcare, PSU banks and infrastructure, which sit in the “leading” quadrant.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 3,114.68 crore today, extending a four‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 392.2 crore, marking a second consecutive day of outflows. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.67 for Nifty, indicating more put (bearish) interest, with the max‑pain level at 23,250 and a call wall at 24,000. Bank Nifty’s PCR is near 1.0 (0.96), suggesting balanced sentiment, with max‑pain at 55,500 and a call wall at 57,000.

Watch the Nifty’s support at 23,032.77 (S1) and resistance at 23,145.77 (R1); a break below 23,032 could test the 20‑day moving average (≈23,000). For Bank Nifty, the key levels are 54,489 (S1) and 54,778 (P). Keep an eye on upcoming earnings from major banks and pharma firms, and any news on FII flows, which could influence the next session’s direction. (PCR = put‑call ratio, a measure of option‑side bias.)
